answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a scarce vouching graph: each established agent may sponsor only two newcomers per epoch, staking part of its own reputation on each one, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Creating a thousand fake identities would require a thousand trusted sponsors, not just free signups. Like quartz forming only under sustained pressure, trust must crystallize slowly through attested work; a nebula of fresh accounts appearing from nowhere earns no weight, and a dune of identical newcomers shifting together is easy for peers to spot and quarantine.
